settings.approvalBrokerScopeHint: Only the OpenCode permission flow goes through the broker. Codex and CodeBuddy in Agent mode never ask for approvals at all; other harness flows keep their manual cards.
settings.approvalBrokerSafetyHint: By default the broker never auto-approves writes, edits, network access, secrets or git writes; only with the opt-in workspace_edits scope may the advisor approve single-file edits inside the workspace during implement delegations (never secrets, CI, git metadata, lockfiles or agent-control files; own daily limit, audited). Advisory requests (advise_all) send by default only a minimal payload (request id, controlled action name, local risk, categories — no command, no resource names). The opt-in “Include redacted command text” toggle adds a bounded, redacted command snippet and basenames only for lower-risk advisory requests; high/unknown risk and sensitive categories (secrets, network, privilege, destructive, expansion) stay minimal even when the toggle is on. Authority requests (low_only / advisor_assessed / workspace_edits) always send the documented redacted tuple; the toggle does not affect them. Redaction is best-effort, not a guarantee; the provider may retain what it receives.
settings.approvalBrokerModeHint: off — manual only (default). shadow — record a recommendation without replying. local_reads — auto-approve only safe read-only actions.

High risk, network, secrets, privilege and destructive actions always stay with you. workspace_edits — the advisor also approves single-file edits inside the workspace during implement delegations only; it excludes .git, data, secrets, CI and lockfiles and has its own daily limit.

settings.browserExternalGuideTitle: How to connect Chrome on your PC
settings.browserExternalGuideIntro: Cretli can drive your own Chrome instead of its headless Chromium: you see what the agent does and can sign in to pages yourself.
settings.browserExternalGuideStep1: Close Chrome and start it with a remote debugging port and a separate profile folder (Chrome refuses remote debugging on the default profile):
settings.browserExternalGuideStep2: Check that the port answers: open this address in that Chrome or run curl on the Cretli machine. It should return JSON with "webSocketDebuggerUrl".
settings.browserExternalGuideStep3: Enter the address in "Chrome debugging address" above and press "Check and save". Cretli verifies the endpoint and switches without a restart. CRETLI_BROWSER_CDP_URL in .env still works and takes precedence.
settings.browserExternalGuideStep4: Tick "Allow Cretli to control my external Chrome profile" above and save the policy. The consent is per workspace.
settings.browserExternalGuideStep5: Open the Browser panel in a chat: Cretli opens its own tab in that Chrome and closes only that tab; your other tabs stay untouched.
settings.browserExternalGuideWsl: In the default NAT network mode WSL cannot reach Windows localhost, and Chrome listens only on localhost, usually on IPv6 [::1]. Forward the port on the WSL virtual interface of Windows.
settings.browserExternalGuideSecurity: Anyone who can reach the debugging port controls that Chrome profile, including its cookies. Use a dedicated profile, never expose the port to the network, and close Chrome when you are done.
settings.browserCdpUrlHint: Leave empty to use the built-in headless Chromium. The address is checked before saving and must point to a private, link-local or loopback address. No restart needed.
settings.browserCdpAllowlistHint: Only needed when the address uses a host name instead of an IP; separate with commas.
settings.browserCdpEnvLocked: Set by CRETLI_BROWSER_CDP_URL in .env; remove it there to edit here.
settings.browserCdpSavedExternal: Saved. Cretli now uses your Chrome ({version}).

settings.browserExternalGuideWslTitle: Cretli in WSL2, Chrome on Windows
settings.browserExternalGuideWsl1: In WSL, find the Windows address (the default gateway):
settings.browserExternalGuideWsl2: In PowerShell as administrator, forward that address to Chrome on IPv6 and allow only the WSL subnet through the firewall (replace 172.20.0.1 with the address from step 1):
settings.browserExternalGuideWsl3: Check from WSL, then enter http://172.20.0.1:9222 (your address) above:
settings.browserExternalGuideWslIpv6: Connection reset (curl error 56) means the forward targets 127.0.0.1 while Chrome listens on [::1]: check with "netstat -ano | findstr 9222" on Windows and use v4tov6 as above.
settings.browserExternalGuideWslNoAny: Never use listenaddress=0.0.0.0: it exposes the debugging port, and with it your Chrome profile, to the whole local network. Remove such a rule with "netsh interface portproxy delete v4tov4 listenaddress=0.0.0.0 listenport=9222".
settings.browserExternalGuideWslChange: The Windows address on the WSL interface can change after a Windows or WSL restart; then update the forward and the address above. Alternatively, networkingMode=mirrored in %UserProfile%\.wslconfig (then wsl --shutdown) makes http://127.0.0.1:9222 work directly, but it changes networking for all of WSL.
settings.browserCalmPaceModeHint: The agent works at a relaxed pace: slower clicks, gradual cursor movements and scrolling. Chats receive browsing guidance. Applies after saving, including open sessions; independent of native networking. This does not guarantee passing bot checks.
settings.browserCdpMaxSessions: Cretli sessions in the external Chrome
settings.browserCdpMaxSessionsHint: How many Browser sessions (panel, chats and background agents) may use the external Chrome at the same time. Each session opens only its own tabs; they share the profile's cookies. Applies after saving; open sessions stay open.
settings.browserCdpNativeNetwork: Let Chrome load public pages itself
settings.browserCdpNativeNetworkHint: Requests to allowed public addresses go through Chrome's own network stack, cookies and IP, so sites with bot protection see a normal browser. Cretli still checks every request against the policy, but Chrome follows server redirects without re-checking them. Local, LAN and Cretli addresses always stay on the strict path.

settings.reviewerSelectionHint: Automatic = the model picker chooses each reviewer. Fixed pair = the same two reviewers every round.

settings.delegationSettings_sessionsHint: Models and session continuation. Each switch only affects future starts and only decides whether a new delegation re-enters an earlier chat; model choice stays in the Models tab, reviewer pairs in the Review tab.
settings.delegationContinuationHint: Five independent choices, each with its own scope. Off always means a fresh chat; the stage still runs. Each delegation has a new report, verdict and verification.
settings.delegationHint_plan_session_scope: The same TODO or the entire orchestration, while keeping the same executor and folder.
settings.delegationHint_implement_session_scope: The same TODO or the entire orchestration, while keeping the same executor and folder.
settings.delegationHint_fix_session_scope: The same TODO or the entire orchestration, while keeping the same executor and folder.
settings.delegationField_continue_cross_role_sess: Reuse one chat across code review and implement/fix

settings.delegationHint_continue_implement_sessio: Implementation returns to an earlier implementation chat within the selected scope.
settings.delegationHint_continue_fix_sessions: Fixes return to an earlier fix or implementation chat within the selected scope.

settings.delegationHint_continue_review_plan_sess: Plan reviews re-enter the reviewer chat within the chosen scope. Audit and closure never share a chat.
settings.delegationHint_continue_review_code_sess: Code reviews re-enter the reviewer chat within the chosen scope. Audit and closure never share a chat.

settings.sessionsReviewPairLink: Reviewer selection and fixed pairs (Review tab)

settings.delegationHint_reviewer_pair_members: Two members chosen from Settings favorites, or none.

settings.watcherPhase_implement: Implement: implement, review and fix approved leaves
